title: Conditional-entropy security of combinatorial AONTs under arbitrary priors
summary: Characterize the information-theoretic security of every combinatorial all-or-nothing transform under an arbitrary prior input distribution.

formal_statement.body: For every combinatorial $(t,s,v)$-AONT $A$, every prior distribution on its input $s$-tuples, every set $X$ of $t$ input coordinates, and every set $Y$ of $s-t$ output coordinates, characterize $H(X\mid Y)$ exactly. The characterization must determine the perfect-security case $H(X\mid Y)=H(X)$ and the weak-security case $0<H(X\mid Y)\le H(X)$ for all admissible priors.

scope.domain: Combinatorial all-or-nothing transforms under arbitrary prior input distributions
assumptions: $A$ is a combinatorial $(t,s,v)$-AONT in the source sense
The prior is an arbitrary distribution on input $s$-tuples
Security is measured by the source's conditional entropy $H(X\mid Y)$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves bounds and exact cases when the input coordinates are independent, including non-identically distributed inputs, and recalls the equiprobable and positive-support cases. Arbitrary dependent and non-identical prior distributions remain without a complete characterization.

citations.label: Gu--Akao--Esfahani--Miao--Sakurai, combinatorial AONT security problem

progress.summary: Problem 3 asks for the security properties of combinatorial AONTs for general prior input distributions; the source resolves only restricted prior classes.
